standard.title: Shipbuilding — Mineral Fibre Resin Bonded Slabs — Specification
standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements, materials, manufacture, and methods of sampling and testing for mineral fibre resin bonded slabs used for thermal insulation and acoustic lagging on board ships. It applies specifically to flat surfaces operating at temperatures from -25°C to 350°C.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the requirements, materials, manufacture, and methods of sampling and testing for mineral fibre resin bonded slabs used for thermal insulation and acoustic lagging on board ships. certification.description: Voluntary Quality and Performance Specification. Unlike safety-critical builders hardware or transport systems under mandatory QCOs, mineral fibre slabs for shipbuilding are certified on a voluntary basis. Manufacturers are eligible to apply for a BIS license to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on slab wrapping or tags. However, compliance with this specification is universally required in commercial shipyards, Indian Navy, and Coast Guard procurement tenders to ensure fire safety, structural thermal efficiency, and acoustic lagging performance on flat surfaces.
requirements: Every commercial package, crate, or bundle of slabs conforming to this standard may carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).
Slabs must consist of glass, rock, or slag fibres impregnated with a suitable organic or inorganic resin binder.

Standard dimensions are specified as 1000 mm length x 500 mm width. Preferred thicknesses are 25, 50, 75, or 100 mm. Alternative dimensions may be supplied as mutually agreed between the purchaser and supplier.
The maximum weight of finished slabs must not exceed values defined in the code for each specified thickness (e.g. 1 kg/m² for 25 mm slabs) to manage the ship's overall deadweight.

Slabs are tested for water absorption through partial immersion. A 150 mm x 25 mm specimen is suspended vertically with its edge immersed 6 mm below the surface of tap water for 48 hours. After immersion (and careful wiping of surface water), the water absorption must not exceed the specified limit of 4 kg/m².

To prevent galvanic corrosion on contacting steel bulkheads or aluminum hulls in marine environments, the alkalinity of the mineral fibres must be low, capped at a maximum of 1 percent when tested per IS 3144.

Un-fiberized glassy particles (shot) decrease thermal efficiency. The standard limits shot content to a maximum of 5 percent by mass for particles passing a 500-micron sieve, and 15 percent by mass for a 250-micron sieve. Any individual shot particle must not exceed 5 mm in any dimension.
For fire safety on board vessels, slabs must satisfy Class 1 flammability requirements (low flame spread) when tested in accordance with IS 13286.
To provide adequate thermal barrier performance, the thermal conductivity at a mean temperature of 20°C must not exceed 0.035 W/m°C when evaluated by the guarded hot-plate method of IS 3346.

The binder resin content (impregnation ratio) must range strictly between a minimum of 5 percent and a maximum of 10 percent by mass (tested per Annex B) to maintain structural integrity of the slabs without creating excessive organic mass.
